mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on Team A's corners-FOR split by half (first half vs second half) AND Team B's corners-FOR split by half, comparing the within-match half-level distribution of corners for the higher-generating side (Team B) against the lower-generating side (Team A). This requires both half-level splits for both teams simultaneously — not a single observable with one band.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's corner advantage over Team A is expected to be more pronounced in the second half than the first half, given that Team B's second-half corner rate exceeds its first-half rate while Team A's first-half and second-half rates are more balanced.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B generates substantially more corners than Team A (both for and against), and Team A's corner production is below competition average while Team B's is above. The joint relationship between Team A's corner-suppression tendency (corners allowed) and Team B's corner-generation tendency, examined together across first-half and second-half splits, may reveal whether the corner imbalance is concentrated in one half or distributed across both halves.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is not a single observable with one conditioning band. It requires the joint half-level profile of corners FOR both teams simultaneously — a two-team, two-half asymmetric comparison — which cannot be reduced to one team's observable versus one opponent-descriptor band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on each team's possession FOR average and their shots-on-target FOR average, examining whether the possession-dominant team (Team B) achieves a shots-on-target rate that scales with its possession advantage, or whether Team A's shots-on-target rate is relatively higher per unit of possession than Team B's — an asymmetric cross-observable relationship between the two sides.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The team with higher possession (Team B) is expected to generate more shots and shots on target in absolute terms, but the ratio of shots-on-target to possession share for Team A may be relatively elevated compared to Team B, indicating a non-linear or asymmetric relationship between possession dominance and shot efficiency across the two sides.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A shows a structural possession deficit (averaging ~43% possession FOR, with opponents averaging ~57% against them), while Team B averages ~53% possession FOR. The joint relationship between possession imbalance and shots/shots-on-target differential may reveal whether the team that dominates possession in this matchup also generates a disproportionately higher shots-on-target rate, or whether the lower-possession side (Team A) compensates with efficient shot conversion.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a joint relationship across two distinct observables (possession and shots_on_target) for both teams simultaneously, examining an asymmetric cross-team ratio. It is not reducible to one observable with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the regime shift in Team A's possession (ALL_PRIOR vs RECENT_5) jointly with the corresponding shift in their shots FOR and shots_on_target FOR, to test whether the recent possession increase is accompanied by a proportional, sub-proportional, or supra-proportional increase in shot production — a threshold/non-linear dependence on a continuous observable across two metrics simultaneously.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's recent possession increase is expected to be associated with a rise in shots and shots-on-target FOR, but the relationship between the magnitude of possession gain and the magnitude of shot production gain should be tested for non-linearity or saturation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's recent form (RECENT_5) shows a notable shift in possession profile — rising from a long-run average of ~43% to ~51% — while their shots FOR have also risen recently. Jointly, the relationship between Team A's recent possession regime shift and their shots/shots-on-target production may reveal whether the possession gain translates into a proportional or disproportionate increase in attacking output, compared to their long-run possession-to-shots ratio.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a joint relationship between two distinct observables (possession and shots/shots_on_target) conditioned on a regime shift (recent vs long-run window), not a single observable with one band. The non-linear/threshold aspect of the possession-to-shots relationship adds further richness.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team A's yellow_cards FOR and fouls FOR (as the foul-committing side) alongside Team B's yellow_cards AGAINST and fouls AGAINST (as the foul-drawing side), both benchmarked against the competition context. The mechanism tests whether the combination of a high-fouling team facing a high-foul-drawing team produces a joint elevation in cards beyond what either team's individual card rate would predict alone.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team with above-average yellow cards FOR (Team A) faces a team with above-average yellow cards AGAINST (Team B), the combined match yellow card total is expected to rise above what either team's individual rate against a neutral opponent would suggest — a joint, asymmetric cross-team relationship across two observables.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A accumulates more yellow cards FOR than the competition average and more than Team B, and Team A's yellow cards FOR are higher away than home. Team B concedes more yellow cards against (opponents foul more against Team B) than the competition average. The joint relationship between Team A's foul-committing tendency and Team B's foul-drawing tendency — both measured against the competition baseline — may reveal whether this matchup is structurally predisposed to elevated card volume through a two-dimensional opponent pairing (one team that fouls more, one team that draws fouls more).
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (fouls and yellow_cards) across two teams in an asymmetric pairing (one as producer, one as drawer), benchmarked against a competition context. It is not reducible to one observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on Team A's cards_2h FOR and Team B's cards_2h FOR (second-half cards for both teams), benchmarked against the competition context second-half card average, to test whether the combination of both teams' second-half card tendencies produces a joint elevation in second-half cards. This is a within-match state (second half) conditioned on both teams' second-half profiles simultaneously.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams individually show above-average second-half card rates, the combined second-half card total in their matchup is expected to be elevated relative to the competition context second-half average, with the joint effect potentially exceeding the sum of individual deviations from baseline.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's cards_2h FOR (second-half cards) is notably higher than their cards_2h AGAINST, and both teams have second-half card rates above the competition context second-half average. The joint relationship between Team A's elevated second-half card accumulation and Team B's second-half card accumulation — conditioned on the within-match state of the second half — may reveal whether the second-half card concentration for both teams jointly exceeds what the competition baseline and each team's individual rate would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a within-match state split (second half) conditioned jointly on both teams' second-half card profiles simultaneously, benchmarked against the competition context. It is not reducible to one observable with one band — it requires the joint two-team second-half card relationship.
